why: Mains/low-voltage power introduces electrical safety risks.
whatToDo: Apply harmonised EN 62368-1 or similar safety testing.
Document insulation, creepage, and protective measures.

why: Powered electronics must control electromagnetic emissions and immunity.
whatToDo: Plan EMC testing to EN 301 489 or EN 61000 series.
Include EMC considerations in technical documentation.

why: Wireless selected triggers the Radio Equipment Directive.
whatToDo: Create RF and SAR test plan; engage Notified Body if standards not fully covered.
Ensure spectrum use meets EU requirements.

why: EEE must comply with hazardous substance restrictions.
whatToDo: Collect supplier declarations or perform XRF/chemical testing.

why: General consumer safety duties apply to EU consumer products.
whatToDo: Perform documented risk assessment and maintain incident log.

why: SVHC communication and Annex XVII restrictions may apply.
whatToDo: Check candidate list substances and communicate SVHC >0.1%.
Verify Annex XVII restrictions for intended use.
evidence: Material safety data supporting SVHC review

why: EPR obligations for electrical equipment in EU markets.
whatToDo: Register with WEEE schemes before placing products on market.

why: Battery EPR requires registration and collection scheme membership.
whatToDo: Join authorised battery compliance scheme and report units placed.

why: Packaging waste laws require producer responsibility enrolment.
whatToDo: Register with national packaging PRO and pay eco-fees.
evidence: Packaging PRO contract or registration certificate
